To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
music teacher candidates' educational technology literacy and their attitude towards the use of educational technology are significantly and positively correlated.

music teacher candidates' technological pedagogical self-efficacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge are significantly correlated with each other and technological pedagogic self-efficacy has positive effects on technological pedagogical attitude of music teacher candidates.

there are no significant differences in terms of the levels of educational technology self-efficacy and attitudes towards educational technology use of music teacher candidates according to their gender or class year; however, there are positive and significant correlations between the educational technology self-efficiency and attitudes towards educational technologies use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the attitudes and self-efficacy levels of pre-service music teachers towards education technology.
the relationship between pre-service music teachers’ educational technology self-efficacy levels and their attitudes toward educational technology use.
the attitudes and beliefs of music education students about educational technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the level of educational technology literacy and attitude of the pre-service teachers towards using educational technologies in education are significantly related and that the pre-service teachers have high levels of educational technology literacy.
music teacher candidates have a positive attitude and a sufficient level of knowledge about the use of technology in education.
music teacher candidates’ educational technology literacy levels and attitudes are positively related to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
music teacher candidates' educational technology literacy levels and attitudes are not significantly different in terms of their gender and class levels.
music teacher candidates' attitudes towards educational technology and their self-efficacy levels are significantly correlated.
, the music teacher candidates have high levels of educational technology literacy and positive attitude towards educational technology usage in teaching and learning processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant positive relationship between the self-efficacy and attitudes towards the use of technology in education of music education pre-service teachers.

there are no significant differences between male and female music education students or between the different years in terms of their attitudes towards education technology and their self-efficacy levels in the area of education technology.
the students are not only able to use technology but they are also able to apply the technology to their learning.
